extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, military legal officers, government lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: A legal-digest style reference summarizing authoritative opinions and rules on topics such as the Soldiers' Home, status of inmates, taxation of military personnel and government property, and related military-administrative law. It compiles statutory interpretation and case/opinion guidance for military counsel and administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Inmates not subject to Articles of War
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4824, R. S., subjecting the inmates of the Soldiers' Home to the Rules and Articles of War, is unconstitutional and a dead letter; inmates are civilians occupying dwellings and sustained by trust funds and are not part of the Army; being within the District of Columbia they are subject to District criminal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited opinions: P. 65, 406, Sept. 1892; C. 16062, Mar. 15, 1904; 18342, July 20, 1905; 22730, Feb. 10, 1908; 27456, Nov. 7, 1910. Treat inmates as civilians for applicability of military Articles of War; they remain subject to local civil law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Inmates may leave voluntarily
rubrics_metrics.description: An inmate is not required to remain at the home; privileges may be renounced by acts showing intention to renounce (direct notice or prolonged absence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example case: inmate absent ~22 years after discharge from hospital held to have intended permanent separation and thus ceased being an inmate. (R. 50, 167, Apr. 1886). Use conduct and duration of absence as indicia of intent to renounce membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Funds are trust funds; allowances to officers permissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds supporting the Soldiers' Home are special trust funds administered by the board of commissioners for the benefit of the institution; usage permitting officers of the home to receive and use a reasonable portion of supplies (fuel, light, forage, milk, ice, vegetables) for the home's benefit is not unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held not to be military pay or emoluments and therefore lawful; small annual compensations (e.g., $1,000 to treasurer) from such funds for special services and bonded responsibilities are permissible. (P. 51, 296, Jan. 1892; C. 12965, Jan. 23, 1902). Dispositions of home supplies are within commissioners' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Occupancy of quarters does not preclude other allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: A medical officer occupying quarters at the Soldiers' Home is not thereby precluded from receiving commutation of quarters when ordered to duty elsewhere; quarters at the home are not 'public quarters' at government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance of commutation does not produce double expense for Government and is consistent with law. (P. 56, 174, Oct. 1892). Distinguish ‘public quarters’ from institution-provided accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Transportation advances repayable from pension permissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing transportation to the Soldiers' Home for a needy discharged soldier, with the understanding that the home will repay itself out of his pension when collected, should not be construed as an unlawful pledge of pension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized as repayment by a governmental agency to itself out of funds placed in the soldier's hands by law, rather than a prohibited pledge. (C. 5922, Feb. 1899). Use this mechanism for needy cases where lawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Estates of deceased inmates escheat to United States; Home receives proceeds via Treasury
rubrics_metrics.description: When an inmate dies intestate leaving estate in the District with no relatives within fifth degree, the estate belongs to the United States; proceeds (once turned into money and paid into Treasury by court order) may be appropriated for the Soldiers' Home under section 3689 R. S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home must apply directly to Treasury to obtain funds; Attorney General/US attorney should be informed to collect and turn funds into Treasury. (C. 3498, Sept. 1897). Home cannot itself initiate escheat enforcement but may facilitate reporting of deaths/estates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Board may establish branch; Secretary of War leasing authority limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The original legislation contemplates establishment at one or more places (branch homes permitted); Secretary of War lacks independent authority to grant interests in buildings on military reservations except under the July 28, 1892 statute granting discretionary revocable leases up to five years for public good; if lease permitted, the Home may legally expend its funds to repair leased buildings even if unrecoverable on lease termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three holdings: (1) establishing branches is within original legislative intent; (2) Secretary of War can lease under 27 Stat. 321 subject to limits; (3) expenditures for upkeep of leased buildings by the Home are lawful. (C. 6818, July 1899). Seek statutory basis for occupancy of military property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Home is an agency, not separate legal entity; property title in United States
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soldiers' Home is simply an agency of the United States; title to its property and funds is in the United States and thus the Home is not subject to private attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, private creditors cannot attach Home property. (C. 16767, Aug. 18, 1904). Treat Home funds/property as federal property for suits and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Volunteer Home — Inmates are civilians and receipts reported to Secretary of War
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4835 R. S. subjecting inmates of National Home for Disabled Volunteer Soldiers to Articles of War is unconstitutional; inmates are civilians; under act of March 3, 1891, all receipts must be reported to the Secretary of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulings: R. 30, 286, Apr. 1870; C. 12817, July 2, 1902; P. 51, 104, Dec. 31, 1891. Administrative reporting obligations must be observed even when military jurisdiction does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Homes for Disabled Soldiers — Federal allowance and limited federal oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of Aug. 27, 1888, United States pays money to States/Territories that establish state homes for disabled soldiers; the United States verifies number of inmates but otherwise exercises no inspection or supervision over such State/Territorial homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States entitled to allowances including for inmates who are insane and in asylums; federal role limited to verification. (C. 2222, Apr. 1898; C. 3121, Apr. 1897). Federal funding does not imply broad federal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Officers/soldiers cannot be taxed for pay or property used in military duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities of a State or Territory are not empowered to tax an officer or soldier on account of his pay or for any personal property in his possession properly required for exercise of his office or performance of military duties; pay and emoluments fixed by Congress cannot be impaired by state tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leading authorities and cases cited (Dobbins v. Commissioners; Society for Savings v. Coite; McCulloch v. Maryland etc.). Applies to personal property required for military service (arms, equipment, horses). (R. 30, 215, Mar. 31, 1870; multiple opinions through 1911). Use intent and function of property to determine exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Rule applies to retired officers and soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule exempting officers and soldiers from taxation of pay/property used for military duties also applies to retired officers and soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities extend the immunity to retired status; treat retired personnel consistently where pay/emoluments are federal means to enable national functions. (C. 21469, Apr. 24, 1907 and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Poll tax cannot be imposed on officers and soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: States or Territories may not impose poll taxes on officers and soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the general immunity from taxation interfering with federal functions; apply precedent to poll taxes as well as direct taxes on pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Officers and soldiers taxable for property not military
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and soldiers remain taxable for property that is not military in nature (i.e., not required for performance of military duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between instruments/emoluments used by the United States to execute sovereign powers (exempt) and other personal property (taxable). Consider usage and necessity to determine classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Residence depends upon intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of residence for taxation depends upon the individual's intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard tests of intent and conduct to determine residence for tax purposes; apply to soldiers/officers when assessing local tax liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Former soldiers, pensioners, inmates not exempt merely by status
rubrics_metrics.description: Former soldiers, pensioners, and inmates of Soldiers' Homes are not exempt from taxation solely because of their former service or pensioner status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions depend on specific statutory or constitutional bases; do not presume blanket immunity from civil taxation for former personnel or inmates. (TAX I F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Ex-soldiers not exempt from license fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-soldiers are not exempt from state or local license fees merely by virtue of being former soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License fees are treated separately from pay/property exemptions; state/local licensing authority remains applicable absent specific federal preemption. (TAX I G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of Government Employees — Civilian employee cannot be compelled to work on roads for failure to pay tax
rubrics_metrics.description: A civilian government employee cannot be compelled to perform road work as punishment for failure to pay a tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects federal civilian employees from coercive local enforcement; consult civil-service and local law interaction. (TAX II A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of Government Employees — Civilian resident on reservation liable for school tax
rubrics_metrics.description: A civilian employee residing on a reservation in a Territory is liable for payment of school tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residence on reservation in territories can create local tax liabilities where not inconsistent with federal law. (TAX II B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of Private Property on Military Reservations — State cannot tax government property
rubrics_metrics.description: A State cannot tax property owned by the federal government located on military reservations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow principles of federal immunity from state taxation of federal property; analyze whether exclusive jurisdiction has been ceded and any reservations in the ceding act. (TAX III A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of Private Property — Prior liens not enforceable after cession of exclusive jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes that were a lien on land when conveyed are not enforceable where exclusive jurisdiction has been ceded to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the terms of cessions of jurisdiction and any reservations to determine enforceability of preexisting local liens. (TAX III B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — United States not compelled to pay local inspection/quarantine fees; may contract for such services
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States cannot be compelled to pay local fees for inspection services or quarantine/harbor regulation, but may enter into contracts to have inspections performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat compulsion as barred by sovereign immunity, but permit voluntary contractual arrangements when appropriate. (TAX III J, K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation — Government instrumentality not subject to state or municipal taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: A government instrumentality is not subject to state or municipal taxation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply broad doctrine of federal immunity to instrumentalities unless specific statute or cession provides otherwise. (TAX III P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Home — Cross-reference procedural/admin matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Various administrative cross-references affecting Soldiers' Home operations: attendant to entering inmate, bonds, contracts with the Home, sale of intoxicants, eligibility of retired soldiers, taxation of inmates, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cross-referenced sections (Bonds I H 2; Contracts XVI E; Intoxicants IV; Retirement II B 6; Tax I F) for procedural and collateral requirements affecting Home administration.
